name: Agreement with the Nez Perce, May 1, 1893, ratified August 15, 1894
aka: Nez Perce cession of unallotted lands
promises: Of the reservation of about 762,000 acres kept by the 1863 treaty, the tribe ceded the 549,559 acres left after allotments and tribal trust lands, for $1,626,222 at $3 an acre as negotiated; the parties later agreed the consideration paid was $1,634,664, about $2.97 an acre (ICC Docket 175-B; 176 Ct. Cl. 815).

breaches.what: After the Court of Claims twice reversed and remanded, the Indian Claims Commission found the ceded land worth $3,022,575 on August 15, 1894, about $5.50 an acre, held the $1,634,664 paid so grossly inadequate as to be unconscionable, and entered a final award of $1,387,911. The Commission had first ruled in 1964 that the price was not unconscionable.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Docket 175-B, 29 Ind. Cl. Comm. 127 (1972), on remand from 176 Ct. Cl. 815 (1966) and 194 Ct. Cl. 490 (1971)

source.title: Nez Perce Tribe v. United States, Docket 175-B, Order Amending Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law (November 1, 1972)
source.publisher: Indian Claims Commission Decisions, Oklahoma State University Library

breaches.quote: was so grossly inadequate as to make the consideration unconscionable

compensation: $1,634,664 under the agreement. The Commission's final award of November 1, 1972 was $1,387,911, without interest after the Court of Claims reversed the interest award in 1971.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says that after the government forced a second treaty in 1863 that cut the reservation to about 750,000 acres, it imposed allotment, which the 1893 Agreement reflected, opening the remaining reservation land to non-Indian settlement and leaving a checkerboard of Indian allotments and non-Indian parcels.

openQuestions: This cession is already a breach on kappler-851 (the 1863 Nez Perce treaty), so sameEventAs points there and the taking is counted once.
kappler-851 was corrected in audit round 14 to the 1972 final award of $1,387,911 after the 1971 reversal of interest (194 Ct. Cl. 490).
A 1973 attorneys' fee finding (OSU id 1188) calls the 1972 award a compromise settlement; the 1972 opinion, conclusions and final award read as an adjudicated award. Recorded as a Commission finding.
The Nez Perce Tribe's account (nezperce.org history, cited on kappler-851) was not reopened in this pass, so no nation voice is recorded here.

plain.promised: In 1893 the Nez Perce sold the 549,559 acres of their 1863 reservation left after allotment, for about $2.97 an acre.
plain.happened: After two appeals, the Indian Claims Commission found in 1972 that the land was worth about $5.50 an acre and that the price paid was unconscionable.
plain.today: The Commission awarded $1,387,911 in 1972, without interest.
